Diagnostics

High Angle of Attack
|α| reached 177.8° during flight — may indicate MPC solver timeouts on ARM64
High Angular Rate
ω reached 4265°/s — tumbling risk
Fin Saturation
Fins at max deflection 17.9% of flight — solver may be computing unstable controls
Poor Servo Tracking
MAE = 3.09° (limit 1.5°) — check servo calibration, backlash, CAN latency
Frequent Large Tracking Errors
53.6% of samples have |err| > 2° — servo slew rate or CAN jitter issue
Servo Feedback Abort Triggered
Simulation aborted 1 step(s) due to feedback loss — CAN bus failure
Servo Feedback Stale Periods
15.7% of steps used last-known CAN angle (stale feedback) — intermittent CAN dropouts
MPC Deadline Violations
mpc_us exceeded 20000us in 100% of cycles — ARM64 cannot meet realtime budget
Servo Delay Under-Compensated
MPC commands arrive too late for servo — increase RKT_MPC_SVO_DLY. Symptoms: roll reached 180° (should be <10°); pitch σ=42.1° in terminal (should be <4°); |α| reached 177.8° (should be <12°); servo tracking MAE=3.1° (servo lagging behind commands); servo tracking P95=9.2° (large transient lag)

Recommendations

Range error is -59.4% — tune MPC guidance gains or verify thrust curve
High in-flight AoA — consider lowering qp_solver_cond_N further or reducing N_horizon
Pitch oscillation in terminal phase — check damping gains and actuator bandwidth
Fins saturating — likely MPC solve timeouts produce suboptimal controls; check qp_solver_cond_N is set (should be ~10, not None)
Servo tracking MAE=3.09° exceeds 1.5° limit — check fin mechanical play, servo_auto_zero calibration, CAN bus speed
Significant CAN dropout — check wiring, connector seating, servo_feedback_timeout_ms in hil_config.yaml
⚠ SERVO DELAY: Set RKT_MPC_SVO_DLY = 0.190s (measured 150ms + 40ms overhead, min 100ms). This gives lookahead_stage=10.
